action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'duo_pose' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'pose': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'duo_hinge' reports the pose, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

pose.description: For 'duo_pose': the pose to move the hinge to.

angle.description: For 'duo_pose' with pose 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

2026-10-21 (saved-key work, branch claude/api-key-saved-state): Kenneth declined computer-use control of the app, and the Remove path's AppConfig code only runs in the real app. What worked in ~2 minutes:

1. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject a `<script>` right after `<head>` that polls for `window.__jusprinBridge`, wraps its `deliver` to `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/log?'+JSON)` the envelopes of interest, and sends page messages with `window.wx.postMessage(JSON.stringify({protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge',version:1,id,type,payload}))`.
2. Serve the dir with `python3 -m http.server <port> --bind 127.0.0.1 > server.log`; the request log is the test output.
3. Launch the built binary directly: `JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/page.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with real *_api_key items deleted and TESTONLY keys added>`. The endpoint override keeps model-list and chat traffic off the real providers.
4. Read the data dir's JusPrin2.conf afterwards for persisted effects; delete the scratch data dir.

The fork's app bundle id is `io.jusprin.JusPrin` (not com.softfever3d.orca-slicer as [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] says). Related: [[fake-host-page-fixture]] (page-only states), [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

**Screenshots without screen control (2026-10-21):** add a `snap` command that POSTs `document.documentElement.outerHTML` (mark `document.activeElement` with `data-visual-focus` first) to a tiny local receiver, then strip `<script>`s, replace `:focus-visible` with `[data-visual-focus]`, pin `html,body` to the captured width (headless Chrome has a minimum window width) and screenshot. Keep the page running: the web view's timers stop ~10 s after the window loses visibility, so front the app by pid with `osascript … set frontmost` before every step and run `caffeinate -u -d -t 600`. The app follows the macOS appearance, not `dark_color_mode`; for dark captures deliver an `appearance: dark` envelope to the page and reapply it after any full `state` (a chat turn resends it). A stand-in provider (`JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` → local server that hangs while a flag file exists, else answers 401) produces "checking" and "rejected" for real.

modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:04.144Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. After a relaunch with no debugger the same slice ran at once. Suspected trigger: pausing the app while its thread pool was starting. Don't report such a hang as an app bug without a run that had no debugger attached.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect JusPrin's own interface text into its translation catalogs.

JusPrin keeps its translations apart from OrcaSlicer's, so taking a new
OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a catalog:

  * native/JusPrin.pot and native/<lang>.po hold the text the native windows
    mark with _L, _u8L, L, _L_CONTEXT and _L_PLURAL under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin.
    Text OrcaSlicer's own template already has is left out: its translations
    come from upstream. Brand/brand_catalogs.py merges these into the catalog
    the app loads.
  * pages/<lang>.po hold the text of the AI and Home pages, marked with the
    Lingui macros (t, Trans, Plural). Lingui's own extractor writes them.

Run it after marking or changing text, then translate the new entries:

    python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

Needs GNU gettext (xgettext, msgmerge, msgcat, msgcomm) and the pages'
node_modules (npm ci in AgentUI).
"""

import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
JUSPRIN = HERE.parent
ROOT = JUSPRIN.parents[3]
UPSTREAM_I18N = ROOT / "localization" / "i18n"
NATIVE = HERE / "native"
PAGES = HERE / "pages"

# The keywords upstream's scripts/run_gettext.sh passes, translated_plural
# from Support/Translate.hpp, plural_title from Agent/ActivityTitle.hpp and
# plural_words from Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp.
XGETTEXT_KEYWORDS = [
    "--keyword=L", "--keyword=_L", "--keyword=_u8L",
    "--keyword=L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_L_CONTEXT:1,2c", "--keyword=_u8L_CONTEXT:1,2c",
    "--keyword=_L_PLURAL:1,2", "--keyword=translated_plural:1,2", "--keyword=plural_title:1,2", "--keyword=plural_words:1,2",
]
# Test doubles and the page projects are not native interface text.
SKIP_DIRS = {"Testing", "AgentUI", "HomeUI", "WebShared", "node_modules", "Localization"}

DATE = re.compile(r'^"POT-Creation-Date: .*\\n"\n', re.M)


def languages():
    data = json.loads((HERE / "languages.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return [l["code"] for l in data["languages"] if l["code"] != data["source"]]


def run(*args, **kw):
    subprocess.run(list(args), check=True, **kw)

# Failures the person can fix, no longer shown as "Something went wrong on our side"

Nothing is committed or pushed. The app change sits uncommitted in the JusPrin worktree
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fixable-errors-specific`, on branch
`claude/fixable-errors-specific`, cut from `jusprin-dev` at 3c27e9b3a0. The server change sits uncommitted
in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, in three files under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/`.

## What changed

App (own AI key: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter):
- An own account out of credits now says "Your <service> account is out of credits. Add credits at
  <service>, then try again." This covers the answer before the reply and an error event inside the reply
  (OpenAI sends the latter after HTTP 200, as Sentry JUSPRIN-APP-4 shows). It applies to the chat and to
  Check key. The error code is `provider_credits_exhausted`, separate from the JusPrin account's
  `credits_exhausted`, because that code shows JusPrin's "Get more credits" button. The sentence is not
  approved by Kenneth yet.
- Anthropic's 403 `permission_error` now reads as "key was rejected". OpenAI's and OpenRouter's 403s
  stay generic: their docs give causes the person can't fix by changing the key (country, guardrail,
  moderation).
- A chat too long for the model reads as the existing "too large" sentence. It is recognized by
  OpenAI's code `context_length_exceeded`, OpenRouter's `error_type`, Anthropic's "prompt is too long",
  and Anthropic's many-image size refusal, either before or inside a reply.
- A JusPrin-account reply that fails mid-way with `request_too_large` reads as "too large". Any other
  code the gateway sends mid-reply is still reported.
- An attached picture whose bytes are not PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP is refused at attach time with the
  existing "This file type can't be read by AI." A HEIC photo named .jpg is an example. A picture is
  now labelled by its bytes, not its extension.
- Windows: saving a file whose name has characters outside the system code page no longer throws
  (`Support/Files.cpp`).

Server (gateway.py): a provider's HTTP 400, or a failed-response event inside the reply, that names a
chat too long now becomes the gateway's existing `request_too_large`, not a reported 500. Every other 400
is still reported.

## Evidence

- Real app against a local stand-in that replays each service's documented answer. Unfixed build:
  every case showed "Something went wrong on our side", except OpenAI's 429 credits answer, which showed
  "rate limited, try again shortly". Fixed build: each shows the sentences above. OpenAI's 403

- agent_bridge_tests pass: 622 cases. jusprin_tests pass: 200. The page catalog and wording tests pass: 47.
  All 22 native catalogs pass msgfmt. Server: 80 gateway tests and 327 jusprin.v2 tests pass.
- Windows file name: the unit test failed before the fix and passed after, on the GCP Windows VM.

- The new sentence needs Kenneth's yes. Its translations are marked `# AI Translated`; Basque and
  Hungarian also carry `# Needs human review`.
- Same Windows `.string() + ".tmp"` pattern, not fixed: AgentHost.cpp near line 3959,
  ProjectPersistence.cpp near line 344 and GcodeHistoryRecorder.cpp near line 146 (data-folder paths;
  it breaks for a Windows user name outside the code page).
- A memory card removed while saving to print history (Windows): not reproducible on the VM, nothing

  fx-before and fx-after.

content.text:
I've fixed the failures the person can act on: they now get a sentence that tells them what to do, not "Something went wrong on our side". The app changes are uncommitted in the JusPrin worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/fixable-errors-specific` (branch `claude/fixable-errors-specific`, from `jusprin-dev` at 3c27e9b3a0). The server change is uncommitted in three files under `web_ent/jusprin/v2/` in tsd-enterprise. Nothing is pushed.

**Decision needed:** what should JusPrin say when the person's own AI key is out of credits? It needs your yes because it's a new message the person reads. There are three options:
- Approve the sentence it shows now: "Your OpenAI account is out of credits. Add credits at OpenAI, then try again." It is in 22 languages and costs nothing more.
- Give me different wording, which means redoing the translations.
- Keep the generic message, so people keep getting a sentence that hides an easy fix.

I'd approve it as written. Do you approve this sentence?

**Before and after, per item.** I tested in a copy of the old build and a copy of the new build, each against a local server that replays each service's documented answer.
1. **Own key out of credits.** OpenAI's error inside a reply, OpenRouter's 402, Anthropic's 402 and Anthropic's "credit balance too low" all showed the generic sentence before. OpenAI's 429 credits answer showed "rate limited, try again shortly". All of them now show the new sentence, in the chat and in Check key.
2. **Key refused with 403.** Anthropic's 403 means the key lacks permission, per its docs. It showed the generic sentence and now says the key was rejected. OpenAI's and OpenRouter's 403s stay generic and reported, because their docs list causes a new key doesn't fix, such as an unsupported country.
3. **Chat too long for the model.** OpenAI's 400 and a too-long failure inside a reply showed the generic sentence. They now show the existing "too large" sentence. Anthropic's versions are covered by unit tests only.
4. **Server, a provider's 400.** A 400 that names a chat too long now goes back as the existing `request_too_large`, not a reported 500. Other 400s are still reported. Separately, the app now refuses an attached picture whose bytes aren't PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, with the existing "can't be read by AI" sentence. That's a HEIC photo named .jpg, for example.
5. **Server, errors inside a reply.** A too-long chat failing inside the reply becomes `request_too_large`, and the app reads that one code. Everything else is still reported.
6. **Windows, memory card removed.** I couldn't make this happen: the "not there" errors already read correctly on the Windows VM. Nothing changed.
7. **Windows, file name outside the system code page.** The test failed before the fix and passes after, on the VM. I did not test dropping such a file onto the real Windows app.

**Tests:** all pass.
- 622 agent tests, 200 JusPrin unit tests, and 47 catalog and wording tests.
- msgfmt on all 22 catalogs, and the clang-tidy include check on the changed files.
- 327 server tests, 80 of them on the gateway.

**Still open:**
- Basque and Hungarian translations are flagged for human review.
- The same Windows file-name problem exists in three more places I didn't fix: `AgentHost.cpp` near line 3959, `ProjectPersistence.cpp` near 344 and `GcodeHistoryRecorder.cpp` near 146. They break for a Windows user name outside the code page.
- When the key runs out mid-reply, the person's message stays in the chat.
- The Windows VM still has my worktree and two scheduled tasks, `fx-before` and `fx-after`.

My notes for the other sessions are in `fixable-errors-specific.md` in the shared notes folder.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool.
